Plot the sensitivity of the results to the grid

Source: R/plot-grid.R
plot.bef_grid_comparison.Rd

The plot() method for a comparison created by compare_efron_grids() shows one row per specification, so that you can see how the results change with the grid. Each row shows the estimated density of \(g\) with its pointwise posterior band, the posterior means of the mean and of the standard deviation of \(g\), and the posterior means and intervals of the effects of the selected sites. Read down a column to see what changes when the range, the number of grid points or the number of spline functions is varied.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bef_grid_comparison'
plot(x, scale = 1, ...)

Arguments

x

A bef_grid_comparison object created by compare_efron_grids().

scale

Multiplier for the values on the effect axis, a positive number. For example, scale = 100 shows differences in proportions as percentage points.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The specifications are shown in the order in which they were fitted, with the first at the top. They are labeled by the settings that differ between them; in these labels, "rule" means the grid method. A specification whose fit failed still has a row, which is labeled as failed and is otherwise empty.

All densities are plotted on the same vertical scale, so their heights can be compared between rows, but the scale itself is not shown. To avoid exaggerating small differences between specifications, the axis for the mean of \(g\) is at least as wide as the standard deviation of \(g\), and the axis for the standard deviation starts at zero.

The sites are those selected with the sites argument of compare_efron_grids(). By default these are the sites with the smallest and the largest estimates, whose effects depend most on the limits of the grid.

See also

compare_efron_grids(), plot.bef_grid(), vignette("choosing-a-grid")

Examples

# Three ranges for the 19 teacher expectancy studies, stored with the
# package. The examples of compare_efron_grids() show the call that made
# the comparison.
comparison <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "raudenbush_ranges.rds",
                                  package = "bayesEfron"))
comparison[, c("expansion", "lower", "upper", "sd_g", "site_4")]
#> <bef_grid_comparison> 3 specifications, best first
#> 
#>  expansion  lower upper  sd_g site_4
#>       0.50 -1.070  1.93 0.314  0.663
#>       0.25 -0.695  1.56 0.317  0.782
#>       1.00 -1.820  2.68 0.297  0.442

# As the range widens, the mean of study 4 moves toward the others.
plot(comparison)
